head.citation-title: Mechanistic insights into CO2 nanobubble-enhanced short-term wet carbonation of recycled concrete fines
head.abstracts: © 2025Conventional wet carbonation processes suffered from low carbon dioxide (CO2) solubility and limited carbonate ion (CO32-) availability, which significantly limited CO2 utilization and carbonation efficiency in recycled concrete fines (RCFs). This study proposed using CO2 nanobubble water (CNBW) as an innovative medium for enhanced ion transport. The physicochemical properties of CNBW during three short-term carbonation processes were systematically investigated, and the optimal liquid-to-solid ratio for CNBW and RCFs was established. The calcium carbonate (Cc) precipitation rate, CO2 utilization efficiency, composition, micromorphology, and water absorption of carbonized RCFs (CRCFs) were evaluated. The reaction mechanism of CO2 nanobubbles (CNBs) in these processes was elucidated. The results indicated that a liquid–solid ratio of 12 produced the highest reaction activity. It achieved a maximum CO2 utilization efficiency of 85.5 % and a Cc precipitation rate of 3.92 % within 15 min. Following carbonation, small Cc particles and their agglomerates formed a dense passivation layer that refined CRCFs’ pore structure. This phenomenon was attributed to CNBs adding additional nucleation sites, which accelerated the nucleation and growth of Cc. The bubble bridging effect promoted the aggregation of Cc particles into agglomerates to form a passivation layer. The cavitation effect of bubbles and the liquid phase vortex action removed loose Cc particles. This process further contributed to forming a dense passivation layer.

coredata.dc:description: Conventional wet carbonation processes suffered from low carbon dioxide (CO2) solubility and limited carbonate ion (CO32-) availability, which significantly limited CO2 utilization and carbonation efficiency in recycled concrete fines (RCFs). This study proposed using CO2 nanobubble water (CNBW) as an innovative medium for enhanced ion transport. The physicochemical properties of CNBW during three short-term carbonation processes were systematically investigated, and the optimal liquid-to-solid ratio for CNBW and RCFs was established. The calcium carbonate (Cc) precipitation rate, CO2 utilization efficiency, composition, micromorphology, and water absorption of carbonized RCFs (CRCFs) were evaluated. The reaction mechanism of CO2 nanobubbles (CNBs) in these processes was elucidated. The results indicated that a liquid–solid ratio of 12 produced the highest reaction activity. It achieved a maximum CO2 utilization efficiency of 85.5 % and a Cc precipitation rate of 3.92 % within 15 min. Following carbonation, small Cc particles and their agglomerates formed a dense passivation layer that refined CRCFs’ pore structure. This phenomenon was attributed to CNBs adding additional nucleation sites, which accelerated the nucleation and growth of Cc. The bubble bridging effect promoted the aggregation of Cc particles into agglomerates to form a passivation layer. The cavitation effect of bubbles and the liquid phase vortex action removed loose Cc particles. This process further contributed to forming a dense passivation layer.
coredata.dc:title: Mechanistic insights into CO2 nanobubble-enhanced short-term wet carbonation of recycled concrete fines
